definition: In this social-psychology context, an advertisement is a message shown to people to influence their views, such as a political campaign message. The packet specifically describes an advertisement as exposure to a campaign message whose wording affected perceptions of a public figure and of people with criminal records more broadly.

reasons: The definition’s general claim that an advertisement is “a message shown to people to influence their views” is not explicitly stated in the packet text; the packet only discusses exposure to political campaign advertisements and subsequent effects on perceptions.

The definition adds that the packet “specifically describes an advertisement as exposure to a campaign message whose wording affected perceptions of a public figure and of people with criminal records more broadly,” which is broadly consistent with the packet, but the overall definition is not confined to the packet-supported characterization because of the unsupported general-purpose influence framing.

The definition makes an unsupported generalization that an advertisement is broadly any message shown to influence views; the packet only supports a specific political campaign advertisement used in a survey experiment.
The packet supports “campaign message” only in this article-specific context, not a general social-psychology definition of advertisement.
The second sentence goes beyond the packet by framing the study’s findings as part of the term’s meaning rather than as a study result.
